boardStatus.blueprintScope: The 2026-effective WQE outline, revised March 2025, has nine domains: Lens and Cataract 13%; Cornea, External Disease, and Anterior Segment 13%; Glaucoma 14%; Neuro-Ophthalmology 10%; Oculofacial, Plastics, and Orbit 10%; Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus 10%; Refractive Management and Optics 8%; Retina, Vitreous, and Intraocular Tumors 15%; Uveitis 8%. Oral exam is case-based across six areas: anterior segment; optics/visual physiology/refractive correction; pediatrics/strabismus; external eye/adnexa; neuro-ophthalmology/orbit; posterior segment. Board blueprint is not a residency syllabus or pass predictor.

boardStatus: This is an ACGME-accredited clinical fellowship specialty track at Johns Hopkins (official page verified 2026-10-07). boardEligibilityNotice: Educational self-study confers no eligibility. ABPath 2026 Booklet of Information: candidate must be certified in ABPath AP/CP, AP, or CP, or ABMGG-certified (ABMGG route: physician diplomates only), and complete 12 months of ACGME-accredited MGP training. ABMGG FAQ says MGP subspecialty candidates need initial Clinical Genetics and Genomics certification or ABPath certification. Johns Hopkins page separately says MD/DO or equivalent and prior ACGME-accredited general pathology (AP and/or CP) or medical genetics; it notes exceptional PhD applicants with extensive clinical laboratory experience may be considered. That PhD exception is not proof of physician status or board exam eligibility.
